newsitem.title: USA: BOXING-DE LA HOYA KEEPS TITLE WITH SECOND ROUND KNOCKOUT.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-DE LA HOYA KEEPS TITLE WITH SECOND ROUND KNOCKOUT.

text.p: Oscar de la Hoya displayed some impressive punching power on Saturday in knocking out David Kamau of Kenya in the second round to retain his World Boxing Council welterweight title.

De la Hoya knocked down Kamau early in the second round and put him down again with six seconds left to improve his perfect record to 25-0, while handing the Kenyan challenger only his second loss in 31 professional fights.
The decisive victory should help quiet critics who have attacked de la Hoya's lack of power following a pair of decision victories.
But unlike in his previous bout, when de la Hoya had to chase Pernell Whitaker all over the ring, Kamau chose to trade punches with de la Hoya, which turned out to be a fatal error.
"I figured if Oscar could get in close and get him in exchanges, he would beat him to the punch because Oscar's hands are much faster," said de la Hoya's new trainer, the veteran Emanuel Steward.
"The slugging really turned out to be to our advantage because of Oscar's speed," Steward said.
On the first knockdown, de la Hoya dropped Kamau with a short, hard left hook to the head.
The champion had landed a left hook seconds earlier and instead of covering up, Kamau came right back in at de la Hoya and took the punch that put him down.
"Everything was set up by the left hook," the champion said. "My left hook is a power punch."
The challenger got back to his feet almost immediately and went right back to the centre of the ring for some toe-to-toe exchanges.

Late in the round, the two again exchanged big punches before de la Hoya unleashed a head-snapping left hook to the side of the head that left Kamau stunned on his feet for a few seconds before he fell over backwards.
Kamau tried in vain to get up and was counted out by the referee at 2:56 of the second round.
"Once I went in I threw some combinations, I landed a good punch," said the American golden boy, who kept alive his date for a big-money bout with Hector Camacho.
"This is a bid confidence boost for me because Kamau has never been knocked out," de la Hoya said.
On the undercard, WBC super featherweight champion Genaro Hernandez barely retained his crown with a narrow split-decision victory over top contender Anatoly Alexandrov of Kazakhstan.
Hernandez improved to 36-1-1, while Alexandrov fell to 30-3.
Hernandez, whose only career loss was to de la Hoya, was the winner by 116-113 on two judges' cards. The third judge scored the fight 115-113 in favour of Alexandrov.
